nodes.note: The large-n exclusion from D>=2^n-1 and the denominator bound from D>b^(n-1) are separate deductions: a solver can establish either without the other. Split them into two bounding claims.

Symmetry and strict coordinatewise monotonicity are distinct properties that a solver can establish separately. The searches only need monotonicity, so remove the unused symmetry assertion or separate it.

The exact starting corner and root bound, and moving both pointers immediately after equality, prescribe one staircase implementation. State the complete level-set enumeration by monotone row/column elimination, and put these particular initialization and update choices in accept.

Choosing the smallest prime factor and the exact floor-root bound is one implementation of the short-block search; other sufficiently small divisors k of n and conservative denominator bounds give the same complete candidate generation. State that general coverage rule, keeping the smallest-prime-factor choice and its numerical cost bound in accept.

Constructing an order-n element by the particular projection g^((ell-1)/n) and enumerating all order-n elements from a known one are distinct steps; a solver can know the latter without knowing the former. Make the main claim complete enumeration of the order-n witness ratios, moving the projection/sampling construction into accept, or separate construction from classification without requiring one construction formula.

Testing denominator two upfront for every n is an optional early-success optimization and fixes where the exceptional case is handled. State that the candidate set includes the witness-generated pairs and the exception (n,a,b)=(6,1,2), with the upfront denominator-two test only an accept example.

review.hazards_note: H1's reassurance about signed __int128 needs qualification: the separate bounds b<=3981 and n<=59 do not suffice, since 3981^58 is far larger than 128 bits. Safety requires the stronger per-input power bound for already-bounded candidates, or guarded/capped evaluation including bound computations; the reference uses guarded 64-bit multiplication and capping. H3 should be conditional on using factorization, with Miller–Rabin bases and Pollard-rho retry details treated as implementation examples rather than universal requirements. H4 should require a conservative bound containing every feasible denominator, not preservation of every exact root-boundary candidate or exact root correction: when b^(n-1)=m, that b is already infeasible because D>b^(n-1), and safely rounded-up bounds also work.
review.editorial_note: The editorial and reference follow P1: geometric shares, primitive-sum divisibility, small feasible search space, and bounded enumeration with the required minimum. Their stopping condition D(q,1)>m is tighter pruning of the denominator range, explicitly allowed by N3's accept.

review.hazards_note: H4 overstates the requirement by saying that any denominator bound must contain every feasible denominator. Once a feasible denominator b0 is known, a correct search may discard all larger denominators even if they are feasible, as N7 explicitly permits; target-specific bounds likewise need only cover the relevant target. Require bounds and rounding to preserve every candidate that could still improve the answer, and reserve the all-feasible-denominators requirement for an unconditional global feasibility bound. The other hazards are adequate.
